composes.brief_description: The fundamental transfer object for SQL operations.
composes.detailed_description: The Base Transfer Object simply contains an identifier, used for SQL operations and assumed to be the primary key for the associated table. Any subsequent transfer object should inherit from this to enforce the primary key behavior.
composes.name: BaseTransferObject

composes.brief_description: ForeignKey<T> stores only the ID of a related object T.
composes.detailed_description: This allows lazy loading - the full object is not loaded from the database until explicitly requested via the resolve() method. Use this when you want to reference another table without the overhead of loading the full nested object during SELECT operations. Example: struct Vertex3D : public cpp_sqlite::BaseTransferObject { float x, y, z; }; struct RigidBody : public cpp_sqlite::BaseTransferObject { std::string name; ForeignKey<Vertex3D> centerOfMass; // Lazy - just stores ID Vertex3D position; // Eager - auto-loads full object }; // Usage: auto body = bodyDAO.selectById(1); std::cout << "Center FK ID: " << body->centerOfMass.id << "\n" ; // Load the full vertex only when needed auto vertex = body->centerOfMass.resolve(db); if (vertex) { std::cout << "Center: " << vertex->x << ", " << vertex->y << "\n" ; }
composes.name: ForeignKey

composes.brief_description: Container for repeated (one-to-many) fields in transfer objects.
composes.detailed_description: This represents a collection of transfer objects that forms a one-to-many relationship in the database (typically requiring a junction table). T Must be a SingleTransferObject (not another RepeatedField) Example usage: struct Tag : BaseTransferObject { std::string name; }; struct Article : BaseTransferObject { std::string title; RepeatedFieldTransferObject<Tag> tags; // One-to-many relationship }; The constraint SingleTransferObject ensures you cannot nest repeated fields: RepeatedFieldTransferObject<RepeatedFieldTransferObject<Tag>> // Compile error!
composes.name: RepeatedFieldTransferObject

composes.brief_description: RAII-style transaction management for SQLite database operations.
composes.detailed_description: This class provides automatic transaction management with the following features: Automatic rollback if the transaction is not explicitly committed Support for nested transactions via savepoints Exception-safe resource management Usage: Database db( "test.db" , true ); { Transaction txn(db); // ... perform database operations ... txn.commit(); // Explicit commit } // If commit() is not called, destructor will rollback For nested transactions: Database db( "test.db" , true ); { Transaction outer(db); // ... some operations ... { Transaction inner(db); // Creates a savepoint // ... more operations ... inner.commit(); // Releases savepoint } outer.commit(); }
composes.name: Transaction

composes.description: The `MigrationManager` shall provide an `apply` method that returns a `MigrationResult`. On first invocation, `apply` shall create the `schema_versions` table if it does not exist. It shall execute all unapplied migrations in version order against a cpp_sqlite::`Database` instance. Each migration's `up` method shall be invoked with a cpp_sqlite::`Transaction` reference. The manager shall record each successfully applied migration as a `SchemaVersion` in the `schema_versions` table (version: INTEGER, applied_at: TEXT ISO-8601, checksum: TEXT SHA-256). The `SchemaVersion` INSERT and the migration's `up()` shall execute within a single cpp_sqlite::`Transaction` — both succeed or both roll back atomically. If any migration's `up` method throws, the manager shall roll back the current migration's changes via the active `Transaction` (without affecting previously applied migrations) and return `MigrationResult{success=false, error=MigrationErrorCode::MigrationFailed}`. The manager shall not re-apply migrations already recorded in `schema_versions`. Concurrent apply calls are not supported; behavior is undefined if apply is called concurrently.
composes.name: llr_migration_apply

composes.description: The `MigrationManager` shall provide a `verify` method that checks whether the current database schema matches the expected state from all applied migrations. The verify method shall compute a SHA-256 checksum of the current schema by querying `SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table','index','trigger') ORDER BY name` and hashing the concatenated SQL strings. It shall compare this checksum against the stored checksum of the **highest-applied** `SchemaVersion` in `schema_versions`. It shall return a `SchemaVerificationResult` containing a `std::vector<SchemaMismatch>` and an `is_consistent` boolean. If the live checksum matches the stored checksum, the result shall be `{mismatches={}, is_consistent=true}`. If they differ, the result shall contain one `SchemaMismatch` reporting the version number, `MismatchKind::ChecksumMismatch`, and a human-readable detail string. If `schema_versions` is empty (no migrations applied), `verify` shall return `{mismatches={}, is_consistent=true}`. Verify is not required to be thread-safe; its behavior is undefined if called concurrently with `apply` or `rollback`.
composes.name: llr_schema_verification

composes.description: The `MigrationManager` shall provide a `rollback` method that accepts a target `int` version and returns a `MigrationResult`. It shall roll back all migrations above the target version in descending version order. Each migration's `down` method shall be invoked with a cpp_sqlite::`Transaction` reference. Rollback shall remove rows for rolled-back migrations from `schema_versions`. If any `down` method throws, the manager shall abort the rollback and leave the database in its partially-rolled-back state, returning `MigrationResult{success=false, error=MigrationErrorCode::RollbackFailed}`. If the target version does not exist in `schema_versions`, the manager shall return `MigrationResult{success=false, error=MigrationErrorCode::VersionNotFound}`. If `schema_versions` is empty, `rollback` shall return `MigrationResult{success=false, error=MigrationErrorCode::NotInitialized}`. Calling `rollback` to a version at or below the lowest applied version (equivalent to full rollback) is valid and shall remove all applied migrations, returning `MigrationResult{success=true}`. Rollback is idempotent — calling `rollback(N)` a second time when no migrations are above N shall return `MigrationResult{success=true}` (no-op).
composes.name: llr_migration_rollback

description: The `MigrationManager` class shall provide a schema versioning system for SQLite databases using the cpp-sqlite library. It shall track applied migrations, apply pending migrations in version order, detect schema drift, and roll back migrations when requested. The manager shall integrate with the existing cpp_sqlite::`Database` class without modifying it. Migrations shall be defined by the user as subclasses of the `Migration` abstract base class and registered with the manager. The manager shall provide a `verify` method that checks whether the current database schema matches the expected state from all applied migrations.
name: Database Migration Manager
